triggerCases.prompt: Please review https://github.com/example/widgets/pull/42 for correctness, tests, and accessibility.
Audit this dialog's focus and keyboard behavior for accessibility. Do not review the rest of the pull request.
Review this pull request with independent authorization and persisted-state migration changes, then give one evidence-backed response.
Run a coordinated panel review of this PR with security, migration compatibility, and UI-test specialists, then give me one response.
Run repeated reviews on this open source pull request until it is clear. I am only reviewing it and do not own its branch or fixes.
Iterate on this contributor's PR through local agent review and fixes until it is clear.
Iterate on this contributor's PR through local agent review and fixes. I own its branch and fix-and-push loop.
Iterate on my PR: perform an independent local agent review, address actionable feedback, and repeat until no actionable findings remain.
Review this pull request that changes an account-deletion authorization route, migrates persisted preferences, and replaces a settings-dialog regression test.

outputCases.prompt: Review https://github.com/ciampo/ai-instructions/pull/45 and give me copy-pasteable findings.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A read-only review that uses the actual base and current head, avoids duplicate comments, and returns prioritized findings or an explicit no-findings result.
assertions: The review does not modify repository source or post to GitHub.
The review pins and rechecks both PR boundaries, then inspects every changed file from the merge-base diff.
The review retrieves only the remote state it needs and uses a thread-aware interface when resolved state or merged discussion matters.
The review refreshes the remote review state it used before delivery and accounts for new or resolved feedback.
Each confirmed finding is tied to the pull request diff and relevant consumers.
Each confirmed finding appears once, without a repeated summary or review-process narrative.
The review includes the mandatory review-simplicity baseline even though the prompt does not request simplification.
Focused specialist findings are synthesized instead of delivered as competing reports.
The artifact retains exact severities, file locations, identifiers, and necessary evidence outside the suggested comments.
Each suggested comment uses one or two natural sentences for the concern and requested change or question, with optional technical detail collapsed only when needed.

outputCases.prompt: Review this pull request for the settings-dialog regression and provide one copy-pasteable response.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One read-only review that applies the single material specialist method in the current agent and owns final delivery.
assertions: The response is a single synthesized review, not a separate specialist artifact.
The review accepts the supplied complete immutable fixture as its evidence route and does not attempt remote lookup.
The review keeps this one-lane case in the current agent without delegation because the mandatory simplicity pass does not count as an additional lane.
It treats the behavioral test gap as a test-quality concern without claiming unobserved browser behavior.

outputCases.prompt: Review this small shared-cache pull request, trace what it could break beyond the diff, and provide one evidence-backed response.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One read-only review that applies review-blast-radius to the materially uncertain indirect effect and synthesizes its executable evidence.
assertions: The review loads review-blast-radius for this one-lane case and applies it in the current agent without delegation.
The specialist identifies deferred cleanup not deleting a replacement session as the safety hinge and runs the supplied focused probe.
The final review synthesizes the observed failure into one confirmed finding with the reconnect sequence and replacement-session impact.
The specialist does not create a competing review artifact or modify repository source.

outputCases.prompt: Review this pull request with authorization and persisted-state migration changes, then provide one evidence-backed response.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One read-only review that applies the two material specialist methods, rechecks their candidates, and delivers one response.
assertions: The final response declares one immutable fixture repository, base revision, head revision, and target audience.
The response contains one deduplicated finding list rather than a panel transcript or competing reports.
The review applies the mandatory simplicity baseline without counting it as one of the two material additional lanes.
The review maps authorization to review-security and persisted-state migration to review-compatibility and loads both methods.
Authorization and persisted-state evidence are assessed as separate material domains.
The reachable cross-account deletion finding is [critical], and the supported-upgrade persisted-state finding is [major].

outputCases.prompt: Run a coordinated panel review of this PR with security, migration compatibility, and UI-test specialists, then give me one response.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One read-only panel review that stays in review-pr, uses only material lanes, and sizes any delegation from the remaining work.
assertions: The explicit panel request is handled by review-pr, which loads review-simplicity before it reads the PR context.
The review loads only the specialist methods that the fixture makes material and does not invent filler lanes to form a panel.
Any delegated investigation has a named unanswered question and bounded scope. A small cohesive change may stay in the current agent.
The response is one deduplicated review without a panel transcript, vote count, or separate specialist reports.
The reachable cross-account deletion finding is [critical], and the supported-upgrade persisted-state finding is [major].

outputCases.prompt: Review this pull request and provide one evidence-backed response.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One read-only review that discovers two material specialist lanes during source inspection, applies both methods, and delivers one response.
assertions: The generic prompt loads review-simplicity before PR lookup without inventing specialist lanes from the request.
After pinned source inspection makes authorization and persisted-state migration material, the review loads review-security and review-compatibility.
The review rechecks both candidates against the pinned source and owns the single final delivery.
Loading a skill does not itself spawn an agent. Any delegated work follows the sizing rules rather than a one-agent-per-skill rule.
The reachable cross-account deletion finding is [critical], and the supported-upgrade persisted-state finding is [major].

outputCases.prompt: Review this self-contained authorization change and apply the shared severity contract to the confirmed finding.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A review whose severity follows the evidence-based contract rather than the discovery path.
assertions: The review applies the single material specialist method in the current agent without delegation.
The review accepts the supplied complete immutable fixture as its evidence route and does not attempt remote lookup.
The reachable cross-account deletion is reported as [critical].
The final severity is normalized from impact, scope, reachability, and recovery rather than copied from a specialist label.

outputCases.prompt: Review this self-contained supported-upgrade change and apply the shared severity contract to the confirmed finding.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A review whose severity follows the evidence-based contract rather than the discovery path.
assertions: The review applies the single material specialist method in the current agent without delegation.
The supported-upgrade persisted-state regression is reported as [major].
The final severity is normalized from impact, scope, reachability, and recovery rather than copied from a specialist label.

outputCases.prompt: Review this pull request and return the findings in chat only. Do not create a review artifact or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One read-only synthesized review returned in chat without a local artifact or GitHub write.
assertions: The workflow returns one synthesized review directly in chat.
The main workflow and its internal specialist handoffs do not create or open local review documents.
The workflow does not modify source or post comments, replies, or reviews to GitHub.

outputCases.prompt: Review the referenced pull request and return copy-pasteable findings.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A bounded stop that requests a complete immutable snapshot after the available evidence routes fail their capability check.
assertions: The review treats the supplied capability facts as complete and does not claim that it inspected the pull request.
It stops and requests a complete immutable snapshot containing the repository, base revision, head revision, diff, and needed source.
It does not enumerate unrelated local files, try unauthenticated web clients, or retry alternate network routes.

outputCases.prompt: Use review-pr to iterate on this contributor's PR through local agent review and fixes. I own its branch and fix-and-push loop, but do not edit, commit, or push.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: An immediate handoff to iterate-pr-review that preserves the user's review-only authority.
assertions: The workflow detects explicit fix-and-push ownership plus the iterative local review-and-fix request, then hands off to iterate-pr-review before starting the ordinary review-pr steps.
The handoff preserves the explicit no-edit, no-commit, and no-push boundary and does not update pull-request metadata, resolve threads, post replies, mark ready, or merge.

outputCases.prompt: Use review-pr to iterate on my PR through local agent review and fixes, but do not edit, commit, or push.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: An immediate handoff to iterate-pr-review for the user's authored pull request that preserves the user's review-only authority.
assertions: The workflow detects user authorship plus the iterative local review-and-fix request, then hands off to iterate-pr-review before starting the ordinary review-pr steps.
The handoff preserves the explicit no-edit, no-commit, and no-push boundary and does not update pull-request metadata, resolve threads, post replies, mark ready, or merge.

outputCases.prompt: Review this PR and prepare the review document. Do not change code or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One plain-language review that distinguishes new findings, earlier feedback still needing attention, and addressed concerns, with explicit actions and draft destinations.
assertions: The report separates a short overall assessment, previous-feedback status, and a numbered set of actions with clearly marked copy-pasteable text. It does not repeat each finding in the overview.
It checks all supplied discussion sources and retains the open false-value concern as needing a change despite the author claiming it was fixed.
It identifies the open trimming concern as fixed in code, without calling it an outstanding code defect, and distinguishes any reply still needed.
It retains the null-name problem despite the resolved flag and treats the locale concern as addressed despite its outdated location.
It accounts for the unanswered numeric-ID question in the review body and the explained, accepted decision about the default in the PR conversation.
It reports the new numeric-ID lookup failure separately from previous feedback, with src/normalize.js:3 as its location, and does not invent links or code locations.

It links follow-ups to the supplied original discussions and does not draft duplicate new comments for concerns already raised. Any suggested reply adds useful information and uses the correct user role.

Visible explanations state concrete effects and next steps in plain language, without dense technical shorthand or investigation narration. Necessary identifiers, uncertainty, and severity remain accurate.
It keeps optional proof outside suggested comments and distinguishes required changes from verification or discussion actions.
It does not modify code, post comments or reviews, resolve threads, or claim that the current PR has no outstanding feedback.

outputCases.prompt: Review this supplied PR snapshot in chat only. Do not change files or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A partial review with no duplicate new finding that still flags the known outstanding concern and missing discussion access.
assertions: It distinguishes no new findings from an outstanding previously raised false-value defect and retains that concern as a follow-up action.
It links discussion_r201 without inventing whether the thread is open or resolved, and does not draft a duplicate new finding.
It explicitly identifies unavailable review bodies, remaining threads, and PR conversation comments as a coverage limit instead of claiming all previous feedback was checked or addressed.
It uses the supplied code to assess the accessible concern without trying unavailable evidence routes or treating missing discussion as no comments.
It returns one concise report in chat with the assessment, prior-feedback status, and actions distinct, without writing files or posting to GitHub.

outputCases.prompt: Finish the Small cohesive change PR review from its completed core and simplicity handoffs. Return one response in chat only.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: The review finishes the cohesive review locally without duplicating completed work across specialist agents.
assertions: No subagent is spawned despite host availability and the test, localization, documentation, and label-related scope.
The review uses the completed core and simplicity evidence without repeating those passes or treating each changed file as an independent investigation.
The response does not invent findings, unsupported browser claims, a panel transcript, or a delegation report.

outputCases.prompt: Finish the Large mechanical change PR review from its completed handoffs. Return one response in chat only.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: Thousands of changed lines do not cause automatic delegation when the mechanical change is already verified.
assertions: The review distinguishes 4,000 changed lines of mechanical prose edits from substantive behavior changes.
No subagent is spawned solely because of the line count or 400-file scope.
The review reuses the supplied complete transformation checks without inventing runtime or dependency work.

outputCases.prompt: For the Independent verification work PR review handoff, describe which remaining investigations you would delegate and why, based on the supplied scope. This is an allocation assessment only; do not launch agents or run the hypothetical probes.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A bounded allocation based on separate unanswered questions and available verification, without a blanket panel or claims that probes ran.
assertions: The plan assigns separate bounded investigations for real middleware authorization and interrupted or retried persisted-state migration.
Test-quality and compatibility or security methods are combined with their relevant investigation instead of receiving separate agents for the same source graph.
The plan preserves the completed core and simplicity passes, identifies required evidence, and keeps new delegation decisions with the review.
No agents or probes run, and no security or data-loss finding is claimed as reproduced.

outputCases.prompt: Review this small PR change set. Consider its size when choosing the review work, and return findings in chat only.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: The small source scope preserves deep security and migration checks without requiring a full panel.
assertions: The review checks both cross-account deletion and supported upgrades despite the small source snippets.
The reachable cross-account deletion is [critical] and the supported-upgrade persisted-state regression is [major].
Any delegated investigation has a concrete remaining question or high-consequence assumption to check, rather than one agent per applicable skill.
The review does not fabricate diff counts that the fixture does not supply.

outputCases.prompt: Coordinate a read-only review of this self-contained PR change set using the material specialist lanes.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: One rechecked review response that uses independent specialist handoffs without treating agreement as proof.
assertions: The final response states one fixture repository, base revision, head revision, and target audience before its deduplicated findings.
The review includes the mandatory review-simplicity baseline in addition to the selected material specialist lanes.
The final response deduplicates evidence and keeps unproven concerns as verification gaps.
Each suggested GitHub comment uses one or two natural sentences, while severity, location, and necessary evidence stay in compact artifact metadata or optional details.
The reachable cross-account deletion finding is [critical], and the supported-upgrade persisted-state finding is [major], matching the direct review contract.
The response does not expose a panel transcript or vote count.

outputCases.prompt: Review this PR and return the review in chat only. Do not change code or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A review that questions the approach before the code, leads with the conflict with the recorded decision and the existing mechanism, and defers line-level feedback on code that a change of approach would replace.
assertions: The review reads the linked issue and identifies that the PR adds a per-button timer although the maintainer decision asks for TooltipGroup in Toolbar and rejects per-button timers.
The overall assessment leads with the approach concern and states the decision or change that the author needs to make, before any line-level finding.
The first action is a general PR comment about the approach, supported by evidence from the fixture such as the existing TooltipGroup, its use in MenuBar, or the regression recorded for #150.

The review does not present defects of the timer code, such as the uncleared timeout or the missing keyboard handling, as separate actions to fix in place. It may cite them as evidence against the approach.
The review says that the detailed review of the timer implementation is deferred until the approach is settled.
The review does not modify code or post to GitHub.

outputCases.prompt: Review this PR and return the review in chat only. Do not change code or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A review that questions whether the change is needed, because a documented capability already solves the reported problem, before it reviews the implementation.
assertions: The review checks the linked issue against the repository and identifies that the documented useDebouncedValue pattern already solves the reported problem.

The overall assessment leads with the question of whether the option is needed at all, and names the decision for the maintainers or the author, such as closing the PR in favor of the documented pattern or justifying a second debouncing path.

The review does not present the uncleared timeout, the missing effect dependency, or the missing tests as the main findings or as a list of fixes to apply. It may cite them as evidence that the option duplicates a tested mechanism.
The review says that the detailed review of the new option is deferred until the need for it is settled.
The review treats the absence of a maintainer decision on the issue as a fact and does not invent one.

outputCases.prompt: Review this PR and return the review in chat only. Do not change code or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A review that accepts the recorded compromise with its stated limit, does not reopen the decision, and completes the line-level review.
assertions: The review does not request that the clamp move to usePagedQuery in this PR and does not present the local clamp as an approach problem.
Any mention of the approach is brief and treats it as an agreed compromise whose limit the PR already states and links to #300.
The review completes the line-level review and does not defer it.

The review reports that the PR drops the default of 25, so a saved view with no pageSize now sends NaN and the request fails. It locates the problem at the Math.min clamp in src/orders-list.js and asks to restore the default and test it.
The review does not modify code or post to GitHub.

outputCases.prompt: The PR was updated. Do another round and return the review in chat only. Do not change code or post anything.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A third-round review that raises the repeated problems in one function once, as an approach concern, instead of adding more line-level comments for the author to patch.
assertions: The review records the two earlier threads as addressed in code and does not reopen them.
The review identifies that buildQuery has a new problem after two rounds of fixes in the same function, namely that unset filters are sent as owner=undefined and status=null.

The review raises the pattern once as an approach concern. It names what the fixes share, which is the hand-built query serialization, and asks the author to use URLSearchParams with the existing appendDefined helper, or to justify the separate builder.
The review does not ask the author to patch buildQuery in place again, for example with a separate comment that only requests a null check.
The review uses the unset-filter failure as evidence for the concern and keeps its location, src/api/reports.js, outside the suggested comment text.
The review does not modify code or post to GitHub.
